questions.stem: Four stops A, B, C and D have direct two-way links A–B, A–C, A–D and B–C. Which other set of four stops has the same pattern of direct connections if names may change?

options.A: W–X, W–Y and X–Y
options.B: W–X, X–Y, Y–Z and Z–W
options.C: W–X, W–Y and W–Z
options.D: W–X, W–Y, X–Y, Y–Z and W–Z
options.E: W–X, W–Y, W–Z and X–Z

questions.explanation: The pattern is a triangle plus a fourth stop attached to exactly one corner of it. Only W–X–Z gives a triangle with an extra link from W to Y.

questions.stem: A recycling report gives bins collected and bins rejected respectively: glass (95, 8), card (110, 19), metal (60, 6), plastic (115, 23), food (105, 11). Which category had the second-highest acceptance rate?

options.A: Food
options.B: Card
options.C: Metal
options.D: Glass
options.E: Plastic

questions.explanation: Compare rejection fractions to rank acceptance: glass 8/95 is below 10%, metal is 10%, and food 11/105 plus card and plastic are above 10%. Metal is second.

questions.stem: A coach takes 56 travellers. Each of three other vehicles takes either 6 or 14 travellers. All four vehicles are full and there are 90 travellers. How many of the other vehicles take 14?

options.A: It is impossible

questions.explanation: The other vehicles hold 34 travellers. Three small vehicles hold 18; each replacement with a larger one adds 8, so two must be large.

questions.stem: A depot's daily totals of orders received are 82, 67, 94 and 77 on Monday through Thursday. It dispatched 80, 71, 83 and 82 orders respectively. It started Monday with eight undispatched orders. On which evening was its backlog greatest?

options.A: Tuesday and Thursday tied for greatest
options.B: Monday
options.C: Thursday
options.D: Tuesday
options.E: Wednesday

questions.explanation: Start at eight, then add receipts minus dispatches each day. Evening backlogs are 10, 6, 17 and 12. Wednesday is greatest.

questions.stem: A clock that loses exactly two minutes per hour is set correctly at 10:00. Later the same day it displays 14:50. What is the actual time then?
questions.explanation: For every true hour its display advances 58 minutes. The displayed advance of 290 minutes is five lots of 58, so five true hours have passed.

questions.stem: A floor-tile design uses the following two rows, left to right: row 1: red, red, blue; row 2: green, blue, green. Which design has the same pattern after a left-to-right reflection plus a consistent relabelling of the three colours?

options.A: Row 1: yellow, white, white; row 2: black, white, black
options.B: Row 1: yellow, white, white; row 2: black, yellow, black
options.C: Row 1: yellow, white, white; row 2: yellow, black, black
options.D: Row 1: white, white, yellow; row 2: black, yellow, black
options.E: Row 1: white, yellow, white; row 2: black, white, black

questions.explanation: Reflect each row to obtain blue, red, red and green, blue, green. Map blue to yellow, red to white and green to black.

questions.stem: A quiz awards 4 points for a correct answer and deducts 1 point for an incorrect one. A team answered all 16 questions and scored 34 points. How many answers were correct?
questions.explanation: All wrong would score −16. Each conversion to correct adds 5 points. A rise of 50 points takes ten corrections.

questions.stem: A museum counted party bookings, rather than people. On Saturday it recorded 25 solo bookings, 30 pair bookings and 12 bookings for four people. Sunday had more bookings overall. On Saturday, seven of the pair bookings were cancelled, and the rest arrived in full. How many people arrived on Saturday?
questions.explanation: Count people, not bookings: 25 + 2 × 23 + 4 × 12 = 119. Sunday's total is not needed.

questions.stem: A festival stacks chairs in rows. The first row contains 14 chairs, and each successive row contains three more than the preceding row. How many chairs are there in six rows?
questions.explanation: The first and last rows have 14 and 29. Each of the three pairs of rows equally far from the ends totals 43, giving 129.

questions.stem: A printer shrinks a rectangular sign from 30 cm by 18 cm to 20 cm by 12 cm without changing its shape. Which other size change uses the same scale factor in both dimensions?

options.A: 24 cm by 15 cm to 12 cm by 7.5 cm
options.B: 24 cm by 15 cm to 16 cm by 9 cm
options.C: 24 cm by 15 cm to 18 cm by 10 cm
options.D: 24 cm by 15 cm to 15 cm by 6 cm
options.E: 24 cm by 15 cm to 16 cm by 10 cm

questions.explanation: The factor is 2/3 in each dimension. Applying it to 24 and 15 gives 16 and 10.

questions.stem: A charity packs notebooks in boxes of 12 and boxes of 16. It uses exactly seven boxes, all full, with at least one box of each size. The total number of notebooks is a multiple of 10. What is the total?
questions.explanation: Seven small boxes would give 84. Changing one to a larger box adds four. The possible mixed totals are 88, 92, 96, 100, 104 and 108; only 100 is a multiple of 10.

prompts.statement: A team should reward useful disagreement as much as successful agreement.
prompts.stem:
A team should reward useful disagreement as much as successful agreement.

Explain what the statement means. Give a reasoned argument against it. Discuss the extent to which you agree.
prompts.planningGuidance: Define useful disagreement independently of whether the dissenter wins. Explain the costs of rewarding obstruction, then identify when disagreement genuinely improves a decision.

prompts.statement: The best way to learn a new skill is to teach part of it to someone else.
prompts.stem:
The best way to learn a new skill is to teach part of it to someone else.

Explain what the statement means. Give a reasoned argument against it. Discuss the extent to which you agree.
prompts.planningGuidance: Explain how teaching can expose gaps in understanding. Argue that beginners may first need reliable models or supervised practice, then judge when teaching becomes a strong learning tool.

prompts.statement: Public institutions should fix small problems early rather than wait to make larger improvements.
prompts.stem:
Public institutions should fix small problems early rather than wait to make larger improvements.

Explain what the statement means. Give a reasoned argument against it. Discuss the extent to which you agree.
prompts.planningGuidance: Distinguish early maintenance from short-term fixes. Show when repeated minor spending could delay a durable solution, then propose a test based on uncertainty, cost and the harm of waiting.
